Thanks for the call today — great overview. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can scope the POC:

1) Integration surface: we want to embed Redwood for: request-level generation (chat), embeddings for semantic search, and a re-ranking step after retrieval.
2) Auth & SDK: please send the recommended SDK setup + headers for short-lived tokens. We run through an API gateway so any header names we should expect?
3) Routing & model variants: we discussed routing by latency vs cost; we need a sample routing policy we can paste into our infra team.
4) Structured output/tool calling: we'll use tool calling for downstream systems — need an example JSON schema and how tool responses are surfaced.
5) Observability: this is critical. Can you confirm the trace-id header you recommend, the list of logging fields Redwood will populate (or that you expect us to provide), and any latency breakdown headers that come back so we can correlate dashboards?

Next steps we propose: tech deep-dive with your SEs + a mutual action plan with dates. Can you share the integration guide and anything security needs for SOC2 review?

Thanks,
John Simmons
Head of Platform Integrations
FinTechCo

John — thanks for the clear recap and for joining today. Attaching our integration guide (redwood-integration-guide.pdf) and a short SDK auth sample (sdk-auth-sample.txt). High level answers inline and then suggested next steps: 

Inline answers:
- SDK/Auth: we recommend using our official SDK (Node/Python/Java) with short-lived bearer tokens issued via your IdP or our token exchange. Header: Authorization: Bearer <token>. For request-level tracing, set X-Redwood-Trace-Id on incoming requests.
- Routing: we'll send a sample routing policy below (David will follow up with a snippet you can drop into your routing layer).
- Structured output/tool calling: we support tool calling and structured JSON output. Example schema attached in the guide — it includes a top-level `tools` array and a `structured_response` field when tool-calling is used.
- Observability: we emit X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown (values in ms per stage), and include X-Request-ID if you don't provide a trace id. We surface per-request logs to the integrations dashboard and can forward syslog/CloudWatch events.

Suggested next steps:
1) Schedule 60-min technical deep-dive with David (SE) to walk SDK, auth, routing, and tool calling (propose Tue 2026-06-16 10:00 PT).
2) Security: share SOC2 artifacts + list of evidence they need. Rishi on cc will coordinate the security packet and SLA discussion.
3) Mutual action plan: David will provide an initial integration checklist + timeline after the deep-dive.

I copied Rishi and Lauren for commercial and security oversight. If the proposed time works we'll send calendar invite.


Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Redwood integration and observability - technical notes & snippets

John — following up with the technical snippets we discussed. Pasting minimal examples here so your infra team can prototype quickly. Full samples in the attached `sdk-auth-sample.txt` and the guide.

1) SDK auth (Node.js):

// pseudo-code
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood.Client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_TOKEN });

// send trace id as header
client.request({
  model: 'redwood-chat-v1',
  input: 'Summarize transaction X',
  headers: { 'X-Redwood-Trace-Id': traceId }
});

We recommend short-lived tokens from your IdP that we can exchange for per-session tokens if you prefer. Always send Authorization: Bearer <token>.

2) Routing policy (example):
- route.primary: redwood-chat-v1 (low-latency)
- route.fallback: redwood-chat-v1-quant (cost-optimized)
- route.rules: if region == 'eu' -> route.primary = redwood-chat-eu-v1

We can provide this as a YAML snippet for your infra.

3) Structured output / tool calling (example response pattern):
{
  "structured_response": {
    "intent": "confirm_payment",
    "entities": [{"name":"amount","value":"$120"}],
    "tools": [{"name":"payments_api","call": {"endpoint":"/charge","payload":{...}}}],
    "raw_text": "Confirmed payment of $120"
  }
}

Tool responses come back in the same request. If you need asynchronous tool invocation we recommend using our webhooks with the request id we return.

4) Observability fields we emit / expect:
- Inbound header: X-Redwood-Trace-Id (string, optional). If missing we generate X-Request-ID.
- Outbound headers: X-Redwood-Request-Id, X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown (e.g., "enqueue:5,compute:120,kvcache:8,postprocess:3" in ms).
- Logging fields (we surface in the integrations dashboard and can push to your logging): request_id, trace_id, model, model_variant, seq_len_input, seq_len_output, latency_ms, cost_token_usd, status_code, error_code (if any).

5) Embeddings / Re-ranker notes:
- Embeddings: send a batch call to /embeddings with your vectors. We return embedding ids and a semantic vector for each input.
- Re-ranker: you can do reranking either client-side (client requests embeddings + reranker model) or server-side using our rerank endpoint as part of the same flow. Server-side rerank (single API call) will add ~20-40ms depending on list size. We recommend server-side rerank for simplicity during POC.

6) PII handling: we can sign a DPA and work with your security team on allowed retention. For POC we recommend tokenization or redaction on your side for PII you prefer not to send. Rishi, we'll coordinate the SOC2 evidence list with FinTechCo.

Let me know if you want the YAML routing snippet and a sample latency-dashboard JSON. I can circulate those before the deep-dive.

Thanks,
David
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks David — that's very helpful. A few clarifying Qs before the deep-dive:

1) For X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown, will values always be ms integers? Can we expect the same keys across model variants?
2) For server-side rerank: what are the limits on list size before latency becomes a problem? We typically return ~200 candidates and want rerank on top 20.
3) PII: we will need the DPA and a statement on whether Redwood ingests any customer PII for telemetry. Is telemetry aggregated or raw?

If we can get the DPA and a short answer on latency breakdown keys ahead of tomorrow's call that'd be great. The proposed time (Tue 10:00 PT) works for us — please send calendar invite.

Best,
John

John — thanks for the questions and for confirming the time. Quick answers and the mutual action plan below. Calendar invite is on the way for Tue 2026-06-16 10:00 PT (we scheduled in your TZ).

Answers:
- X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown: yes, values are integers in ms and keys are stable across the model variants we currently expose (enqueue, compute, kvcache, postprocess). We'll include the exact schema in the dashboard JSON.
- Server-side rerank: recommended flow is to pass up to 500 candidates; reranking cost scales O(n) and for 200 candidates + top-20 extraction we'd expect ~20-60ms additional latency for our reranker on standard instances. We'll profile on your data during the POC and report exact numbers.
- Telemetry & PII: we do not store raw customer payloads for production unless you opt-in for retention for debugging. Telemetry we collect by default is aggregated metrics (latency_ms, error rates, token counts). Rishi will send the DPA and the SOC2 artifact pack to your security contact.

Mutual action plan (high level):
- By 2026-06-18: SE deep-dive complete and routing + SDK prototype created (owner: David).
- By 2026-06-25: Security review completed (owner: Rishi) and DPA signed if needed.
- By 2026-07-02: POC runbook and success criteria (owner: Marissa + FinTechCo).
- By 2026-07-16: POC completion and performance/quality readout.
